title: Northloop Payments Collections Desk: Card Settlement Amount for a Negative Balance
content:
**Rule.** Besides the automatic card charge after the negative balance card charge days, a seller whose payments balance is below zero may settle it by authorising a card settlement against the card on file while the balance has been below zero for no more than the plan's negative balance card charge days; the settlement is booked as one card charge entry and is credited to the balance in full. Once the balance has been below zero for longer, only the automatic charge of the full deficit applies. The card settlement amount is the settlement basis, rounded to the cent. The settlement basis is the deficit, which is the balance below zero taken as a positive amount.

The days below zero are the calendar days elapsed since the date the balance went below zero, the day after that date counting as day one.

## When a seller-authorised card settlement is open

| Days the balance has been below zero, against the plan's card charge days | Seller-authorised card settlement |
|---|---|
| no more than the card charge days | available |
| more than the card charge days | not available; only the automatic charge of the full deficit applies |

## Hypothetical worked examples

- *Payments Weekly (30 card charge days), balance minus 412.37 USD, below zero since 10 days ago.* The settlement is available; the deficit is 412.37 USD, and the card settlement amount is 412.37 USD, credited to the balance in full.
- *Same plan, below zero for exactly 30 days.* Not more than 30, so the settlement is still available. On the 31st day it is not; only the automatic charge applies.
- *Payments Starter (14 card charge days), below zero for 15 days.* More than 14, so only the automatic charge applies.
